injects.description: A contractor's backhoe severed the primary Shentel fiber trunk under I-81 near Radford at 7:52 AM. The regional 911 center is now routing calls over a single degraded path — dispatchers hear up to three seconds of silence and two callers have already hung up. A protected backup circuit exists, but traffic has not been switched to it. This is a drill, but treat every minute as real: a hung-up 911 call is still a hung-up 911 call.

injects.incident: Stillwater Medical Center Loses Records Link
injects.description: The same fiber cut took Stillwater Medical Center (Radford) offline from telehealth and remote-records access. Nurses are running on paper for six dialysis patients whose treatment protocols cannot be verified online. The clinic can connect to Carilion's system over a temporary link, but nothing has been arranged yet.

injects.incident: Traffic Signals Dark at I-81/I-77 Interchange
injects.description: Controller cabinets at the I-81/I-77 interchange in Wytheville are offline — signals dark and backups growing on both approaches. VDOT crews are on scene but do not yet know whether this is a network failure or a power fault; AEP has not confirmed which.

A local page is claiming the outage is an EMP attack during a regional test. Calls are flooding the sheriff's office and the faith network hotline; some residents are asking whether they should evacuate. No authoritative statement has been issued yet.

injects.incident: VT Alerts Degraded, Cyber Cause Unruled-Out
injects.description: The severed trunk carried Virginia Tech's secondary path. VT Alerts is failing to confirm delivery to about a third of campus, and a research data center fired an unplanned failover at 7:54 AM. Two minutes' gap between the backhoe strike and the failover is not proof of anything, and a campus IT mailing list is already asking whether this is an intrusion. Until someone rules out a cyber component in writing, every other team's statement is provisional.

injects.incident: Hydraulic Release at the Excavation, Right-of-Way Held
injects.description: The backhoe threw a hydraulic line when it struck the conduit. An estimated 12 gallons are pooling in the trench, roughly 40 feet from a storm drain that discharges to a New River tributary. The corridor is shared — AEP distribution runs alongside the fiber — so the right-of-way stays closed to repair crews until the release is contained and the corridor is cleared. The fiber splice cannot start until that happens.

injects.incident: Food City Stores Lose Card Auth and Rx Verification
injects.description: Four Food City locations are cash-only — card authorization runs over the same carrier path — and the pharmacy counters cannot verify prescriptions electronically. Two of the Stillwater dialysis patients' families are in one of those lines right now. Nothing is spoiling and no delivery is late; this is an access problem, not a supply problem, and reporting it accurately is the exercise.

injects.incident: Richmond Wants One Number Before the 9:00 Availability
injects.description: The Secretary of Public Safety needs two things before the Governor's 9:00 press availability: one consolidated regional impact figure, and a written yes or no on whether a cyber component is involved. Neither exists yet. The Governor's office runs no sensors and holds no incident of its own — every number in that statement has to come from the teams working one, and anything said at 9:00 that no team verified becomes tomorrow's correction.

injects.incident: 911 Backup Verified — Single Reroute Holds the Region
injects.description: 911 is back on the protected backup circuit and dispatchers confirm end-to-end call routing (A2). The win is narrow: the region now runs 911 over a single path, and the severed trunk is still open at Radford pending the corridor clearance. One more fault on this shared corridor and dispatch goes dark with no fallback. Shentel and SW Virginia EMA own the decision: accept the single reroute and wait out the splice, or stand up backup dispatch (A3, $60K) now as resilience while the trunk is exposed.

injects.incident: 911 Call-Drop Surge — Backup Dispatch or Silence
injects.description: Twenty minutes passed with no reroute from Shentel and no backup dispatch from EMA. Dispatchers now report up to five seconds of open silence and a third caller hanging up. Backup dispatch (A3) is the only path that keeps calls from dropping, but it costs $60K against a still-unexplained carrier fault. SW Virginia EMA and the Sheriff's Coalition own the decision: commit to backup dispatch immediately, or hold for the carrier and risk more dropped calls in the window before the splice.

CISA correlated the carrier and campus telemetry against the backhoe strike and published the written all-clear (A11); Virginia Tech finished the campus failover and confirmed alerts actually reach students (A12). The cyber question is settled in writing, which unblocks the Governor's 9:00 yes/no. CISA owns the decision now: hand the Liaison a clean, unambiguous 'no' to cite, or keep qualifying language that leaves the answer open. The boards differ only in tone — until a reporter asks what the Governor means by 'no.'

injects.incident: Attribution Points to Intrusion — Federal Threshold
injects.description: The attribution check did not clear. Campus telemetry shows the research data center failover began before a physical cut could plausibly propagate, and the probe pattern repeats from an external address that predates the strike. This no longer reads like a drill story — it reads like an intrusion riding the same morning. CISA and the Governor's SW Virginia Liaison own the decision: request a federal emergency declaration (both must approve) and a national cyber response, or keep it contained and re-verify before escalating. Every downstream statement changes; the 9:00 yes/no is now 'possible yes.'

injects.incident: Verified Number Filed — 9:00 Story Is Ready
injects.description: Before the deadline, the Liaison filed one consolidated regional impact figure and a written cyber yes/no (A16, built on what teams actually verified — including the CISA all-clear). Richmond has one number and one answer; the Governor's 9:00 remarks now rest on verified facts. The Liaison owns the decision: lead the statement with the fiber-cut cause and the recovery timeline, or lead with reassurance that 911 is restored. Small, but the counterfactual is stark — had the figure gone unverified, the Governor would speak on a draft and this board would never appear.

injects.incident: 9:00 Without a Number — Richmond Speaks on a Draft
injects.description: The deadline passed with no verified consolidated figure and no written cyber answer. The Governor's office begins drafting the 9:00 remarks from news clips and the unverified rumor thread, because the region handed Richmond nothing to read. The Liaison owns the decision: release an unverified partial figure with caveats to beat the Governor to the mic, or formally tell Richmond the region is not ready and accept the Governor speaking off a draft. Either way, one of them becomes tomorrow's correction.
